extracted.intended_audience: users of the PARI/GP system (interactive GP users and library developers)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for PARI/GP functions (integer/bitwise, object-manipulation, precision/rounding, lifting, random, valuation, and transcendental functions), describing definitions, accepted argument types, edge cases, warnings and library syntax.

rubrics_metrics.name: bitneg(x, {n = -1})
rubrics_metrics.description: Bitwise negation of integer x, truncated to n bits (n >= 0) producing sum over i=0..n-1 of not(xi)2^i. Special case n = -1 means no truncation (infinite leading 1s for negatives).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See behavior for negative arguments (Section 3.2.19). Library syntax: GEN gbitneg(GEN x, long n).

rubrics_metrics.name: bitnegimply(x, y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bitwise negated imply (not(x ⇒ y)) of two integers x and y, i.e. sum of (xi andnot(yi))*2^i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See behavior for negative arguments. Library syntax: GEN gbitnegimply(GEN x, GEN y). Also GEN ibitnegimply(GEN x, GEN y) works on |x| and |y|.

rubrics_metrics.name: bitor(x, y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bitwise inclusive OR of integers x and y computed bitwise as sum of (xi or yi)*2^i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See behavior for negative arguments. Library syntax: GEN gbitor(GEN x, GEN y). Also GEN ibitor(GEN x, GEN y) for |x| and |y|.

rubrics_metrics.name: bittest(x, n)
rubrics_metrics.description: Outputs the nth bit of x starting from the right (coefficient of 2^n); result is 0 or 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Behavior for negative arguments referenced. Examples shown. Library syntax: GEN gbittest(GEN x, long n). For t_INT x, long bittest(GEN x, long n) easier; if n >= 0, low-level ulong int_bit(GEN x, long n) returns bittest(abs(x),n).

rubrics_metrics.name: bitxor(x, y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bitwise exclusive OR (xor) of two integers x and y: sum of (xi xor yi)*2^i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See negative argument behavior. Library syntax: GEN gbitxor(GEN x, GEN y). Also GEN ibitxor(GEN x, GEN y) for |x| and |y|.

rubrics_metrics.name: ceil(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ceiling function: for real x returns smallest integer >= x. For a rational function returns Euclidean quotient of numerator by denominator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gceil(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: centerlift(x, {v})
rubrics_metrics.description: Like lift but t_INTMOD and t_PADIC components are lifted using centered residues: for Mod(a,n) returns y with -n/2 < y <= n/2; for PADIC with non-negative valuation uses centered residue modulo precision; if valuation negative returns pv * centerlift(x*p^{-v}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rational reconstruction is not attempted; use bestappr for that. 'centerlift(x,'v)' alias allowed for backward compatibility. Library syntax: centerlift(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: characteristic(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns the characteristic of the base ring over which x is defined (from t_INTMOD and t_FFELT components).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raises an exception if incompatible primes arise from t_FFELT and t_PADIC components. Example given. Library syntax: GEN characteristic(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: component(x, n)
rubrics_metrics.description: Extracts the nth-component of x counted after initial type code words; for vectors it's the nth element, for matrices nth column, for polynomials nth coefficient (degree n-1), for power series nth significant coefficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer polcoeff for polynomials and [ ] operator for vectors/matrices. Using component requires detailed knowledge of PARI type structure and should almost never be used directly; some exceptions illustrated. Library syntax: GEN compo(GEN x, long n).

rubrics_metrics.name: conj(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conjugate of x; for real quadratic numbers means conjugation in that field. No effect on integers, reals, intmods, fractions or p-adics. polmod is forbidden (use conjvec).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gconj(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: conjvec(z)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conjugate vector representation of z: for polmod Mod(a,T) returns vector of conjugates (complex embeddings if T has rational coefficients; conjugates for intmod coefficients). For finite field elements returns Frobenius conjugates. For integers/rationals returns z; for vectors returns matrix whose columns are conjugate vectors of elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN conjvec(GEN z, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: denominator(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Denominator of x: for rationals/rational functions obvious; for integer/polynomial returns 1. For polmods denominator of minimal-degree representative. For recursive structures returns lcm of component denominators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For polynomials prefer denominator(content(x)). t_INTMOD and t_PADIC have denominator 1. Warning about multivariate object creation and surprising side effects; see Section 2.5.3. Library syntax: GEN denom(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: digits(x, {b = 10})
rubrics_metrics.description: Outputs vector of digits of |x| in base b (x and b integers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN digits(GEN x, GEN b = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: floor(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Floor function: for real x returns largest integer <= x. For rational function returns Euclidean quotient of numerator by denominator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gfloor(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: frac(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fractional part of x, identical to x - floor(x). For real x result in [0,1[.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gfrac(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: hammingweight(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: If x is t_INT returns binary Hamming weight of |x|. Otherwise for t_POL, t_VEC, t_COL, t_VECSMALL, t_MAT returns number of non-zero coefficients/components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples shown. Library syntax: long hammingweight(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: imag(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Imaginary part of x. For quadratic numbers it's coefficient of ω in canonical integral basis (1, ω).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gimag(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: length(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Length (#x) yields: vectors -> dimension (0 for empty), lists -> number of entries, matrices -> number of columns, strings -> number of characters (without trailing null). Defined for arbitrary GP types as number of non-code words (effective length minus 2 for integers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples and notes about awkwardness for nonstandard types. Library syntax: long glength(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: lift(x, {v})
rubrics_metrics.description: Lifts intmods from Z/nZ to Z, p-adics from Qp to Q (as truncate), and polmods to polynomials; if v present lifts only polmods whose modulus has main variable v. t_FFELT and List elements not lifted; meaningless components copied verbatim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lifts performed recursively only one level. Use liftall to recurse indefinitely, liftint to lift only intmods/padics, liftpol to lift only polmods, centerlift for centered residues. Examples illustrate nuanced behavior. Library syntax: GEN lift0(GEN x, long v = -1) and GEN lift(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: liftall(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recursively lift all components from Z/nZ to Z, Qp to Q (truncate), and polmods to polynomials as long as possible. t_FFELT and List elements not lifted; meaningless components copied verbatim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples. Library syntax: GEN liftall(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: liftint(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recursively lift all intmod components from Z/nZ to Z and Qp to Q (truncate). t_FFELT and List elements not lifted; meaningless components copied verbatim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show behavior for mixed objects. Library syntax: GEN liftint(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: liftpol(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recursively lift components that are polmods to polynomials. t_FFELT and List elements not lifted; meaningless components copied verbatim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples. Library syntax: GEN liftpol(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: norm(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Algebraic norm: product of x with its conjugate(s). For vectors/matrices norm applied componentwise (not Euclidean L2). Norm of R element is its square to match complex norm compatibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gnorm(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: numerator(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerator of x: for rationals/rational functions obvious; integer/polynomial treated as rational giving itself; in other cases numerator = denominator(x)*x (applies to vectors, matrices, t_COMPLEX, t_QUAD).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For polynomials prefer numerator(content(x)). Warning about multivariate object creation side effects. Library syntax: GEN numer(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: numtoperm(n, k)
rubrics_metrics.description: Generates the k-th permutation (row vector length n) of numbers 1..n using lexicographic ordering starting at 0. k taken modulo n!.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inverse of permtonum. Library syntax: GEN numtoperm(long n, GEN k).

rubrics_metrics.name: padicprec(x, p)
rubrics_metrics.description: Absolute p-adic precision of object x: minimum precision of components. Returns LONG_MAX if x exact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: long padicprec(GEN x, GEN p).

rubrics_metrics.name: permtonum(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given permutation x on n elements, returns number k such that x = numtoperm(n,k). Lexicographic ordering starting at 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN permtonum(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: precision(x, {n})
rubrics_metrics.description: Two behaviors: with no n returns precision in decimal digits of PARI object x (for exact objects returns largest single precision integer). With n present creates new object equal to x with new 'precision' n (type unchanged). Interpretation of precision depends on type: for real numbers it's number of significant decimal digits; for real/p-adic/power series meanings differ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show use and pitfalls. For exact types no change. For vectors/matrices applied componentwise. For p-adic and power series n is number of significant digits. Methods to test exactness shown: isexact(x) = precision(x) == precision(0). Library syntax: GEN precision0(GEN x, long n), GEN gprec, long precision(GEN x). Note architecture-dependent behavior (32 vs 64-bit).

rubrics_metrics.name: random({N = 2^31})
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns random element in various natural sets depending on argument N: for t_INT uniform integer in [0,N-1]; for t_REAL real in [0,1) with same accuracy as N; for t_INTMOD/t_FFELT random element modulo modulus or field; for t_VEC length 2 returns integer in [a,b]; for elliptic curve ellinit over finite field returns a random affine point (not uniformly distributed over E(k)); for t_POL returns random polynomial of degree at most deg(N) with coefficients drawn from random(leading coeff of N).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses internal generator independent of OS RNG. getrand and setrand available to obtain/reset seeds. Internal generator is Brent's XORGEN algorithm (good statistical properties but not cryptographically secure). Library syntax: GEN genrand(GEN N = NULL). Also GEN ellrandom(GEN E) and GEN ffrandom(GEN a).

rubrics_metrics.name: real(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Real part of x. For quadratic numbers it's coefficient of 1 in canonical integral basis (1, ω).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN greal(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: round(x, {&e})
rubrics_metrics.description: Rounds real x to nearest integer (ties to +∞) and sets e to number of error bits (binary exponent of difference between original and rounded value). If exponent too large compared to precision (e>0) result undefined unless e provided. Operates on every coefficient at every level of PARI object (unlike other truncation functions). Useful to recover exact results after approximate computation when theory implies integer coefficients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples illustrated. Library syntax: GEN round0(GEN x, GEN *e = NULL), GEN grndtoi, GEN ground(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: simplify(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Simplifies x recursively: converts complex/quadratic numbers with integer 0 imaginary part to real; polynomials of degree 0 to constant term; simplifies before arithmetic functions and storing GP results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful before arithmetic functions that expect integers. Automatic simplification occurs unless disabled with \y. Library syntax: GEN simplify(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: sizebyte(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Outputs total number of bytes occupied by the tree representing PARI object x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: long gsizebyte(GEN x). Also gsizeword(GEN x) returns number of words.

rubrics_metrics.name: sizedigit(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Outputs a quick bound for number of decimal digits of components of x, off by at most 1. For exact value use #Str(x) (slower).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: long sizedigit(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: truncate(x, {&e})
rubrics_metrics.description: Truncates x and sets e to number of error bits. For real x chops fractional part; for rational function returns integer part (Euclidean quotient) and e not set. Applies componentwise for vectors/matrices; when applied to power series transforms it into polynomial or rational function by chopping O(X^k); applied to p-adic transforms into integer/rational by chopping O(p^k).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If exponent too large compared to precision (e>0) result undefined and error occurs if e not provided. Library syntax: GEN trunc0(GEN x, GEN *e = NULL), GEN gtrunc, GEN gcvtoi.

rubrics_metrics.name: valuation(x, p)
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes highest exponent of p dividing x. If p is integer, x must be integer, intmod (modulus divisible by p), fraction, q-adic with q=p, polynomial/power series (valuation = min valuation of coefficients). If p is polynomial, x must be polynomial/rational function/power series (monomial case). For vectors/complex/quadratic numbers returns min of component valuations. If x = 0 returns LONG_MAX for exact objects; for p-adic/power series returns exponent of zero.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other invalid type combinations give error. Library syntax: long gvaluation(GEN x, GEN p).

rubrics_metrics.name: variable({x})
rubrics_metrics.description: Gives main variable of object x (variable with highest priority used in x), and p if x is p-adic. Returns 0 if x has no variable. If x omitted returns list of user variables known to interpreter ordered by decreasing priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'if (!variable(x), ...)' to test whether variable attached. In library mode prefer gvar for non-NULL x; for p-adic p is gel(x,2). Library syntax: GEN gpolvar(GEN x = NULL) and long gvar(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transcendental functions (general rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Transcendental functions always return inexact objects (real, complex, p-adic, or power series) with finite precision. Behavior depends on argument type (inexact real/complex: use argument's precision; exact types converted to real/complex using default realprecision before evaluation; polmod evaluated at each complex embedding returning vector; intmod/p-adic only some functions implemented; polynomials/power series converted to power series using series precision).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library mode uses 'prec' parameter rather than default realprecision. For polynomials/rational functions it's advised to convert explicitly to power series in library mode (gtoser) and not to tamper with global precdl. Vector/matrix arguments evaluate componentwise. See individual function entries for branch cuts and other specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: ^. (power)
rubrics_metrics.description: If exponent y is not integer, x^y behaves like exp(y*log(x)); applicable to p-adics as well as usual types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gpow(GEN x, GEN n, long prec) for x^n.

rubrics_metrics.name: Catalan
rubrics_metrics.description: Catalan's constant G = sum_{n>=0} (-1)^n/(2n+1)^2 = 0.91596... (reserved name Catalan).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN mpcatalan(long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: Euler
rubrics_metrics.description: Euler's constant γ = 0.57721... (reserved name Euler).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN mpeuler(long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: I
rubrics_metrics.description: The complex number sqrt(-1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gen_I().

rubrics_metrics.name: Pi
rubrics_metrics.description: Constant π (3.14159...).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reserved name Pi. Library syntax: GEN mppi(long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: abs(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Absolute value (modulus for complex). Exact argument not converted to real before applying abs; can return exact result if possible. For polynomials returns -x if leading coefficient real and negative else x; for power series uses constant coefficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided. Library syntax: GEN gabs(GEN x, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: acos(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal branch of arccos: acos(x) = -i log(x + i*sqrt(1-x^2)). Re(acos(x)) in [0,π]. For real |x|>1 result complex. Branch cuts: (-∞,-1] (quadrant II) and [1,∞) (quadrant IV). Identity: acos(x)=π/2 - asin(x).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See library syntax: GEN gacos(GEN x, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: acosh(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal branch of arccosh: acosh(x) = 2 log( sqrt((x+1)/2) + sqrt((x-1)/2) ). Re(acosh(x)) >= 0; Im(acosh(x)) in (-π,π]. For real x<1 result complex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gacosh(GEN x, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: agm(x, y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Arithmetic-geometric mean of x and y. For complex/negative numbers returns optimal AGM (largest in absolute value over sign choices of square roots). p-adic and power series allowed; p-adic agm exists only if x/y ≡ 1 (mod p) (mod 16 for p=2). x and y cannot both be vectors or matrices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN agm(GEN x, GEN y, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: arg(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Argument of complex number x in (-π,π].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN garg(GEN x, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: asin(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal branch of arcsin: asin(x) = -i log(ix + sqrt(1-x^2)). Re(asin(x)) in [-π/2,π/2]. For real |x|>1 result complex. Branch cuts similar to acos. Identity: i*asin(x)=asinh(ix).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gasin(GEN x, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: asinh(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal branch of asinh: asinh(x) = log(x + sqrt(1+x^2)). Im(asinh(x)) in [-π/2,π/2]. Branch cuts: [-i∞,-i] and [i, i∞] with quadrant continuities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gasinh(GEN x, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: atan(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal branch of arctan: atan(x) = log((1 + i x)/(1 - i x))/2i. Re(atan(x)) in (-π/2,π/2). Branch cuts: (-i∞,-i) and (i, i∞). Relation: i*atan(x) = -i*atanh(i x).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gatan(GEN x, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: atanh(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal branch of atanh: atanh(x) = log((1+x)/(1-x))/2. Im(atanh(x)) in [-π/2,π/2]; for real |x|>1 result complex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gatanh(GEN x, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: bernfrac(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bernoulli number B_x as a rational number (B0=1, B1=-1/2, B2=1/6...). Argument x should be integer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN bernfrac(long x).

rubrics_metrics.name: bernpol(n, {v = x})
rubrics_metrics.description: Bernoulli polynomial B_n in variable v (default x).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples shown for n=1,3. Library syntax: GEN bernpol(long n, long v = -1) where v is variable number.

rubrics_metrics.name: bernreal(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bernoulli number B_x returned as a real number with current precision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN bernreal(long x, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: bernvec(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Creates vector containing Bernoulli numbers B0, B2, ..., B2x as rationals. Obsolete; implemented using repeated calls to bernfrac and uses lots of memory; kept for backward compatibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer bernfrac. Library syntax: GEN bernvec(long x).

rubrics_metrics.name: besselh1(nu, x)
rubrics_metrics.description: H1-Bessel (Hankel) function of index nu and argument x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN hbessel1(GEN nu, GEN x, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: besselh2(nu, x)
rubrics_metrics.description: H2-Bessel (Hankel) function of index nu and argument x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN hbessel2(GEN nu, GEN x, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: besseli(nu, x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Modified Bessel I function of index nu and argument x. If x converts to power series the initial factor (x/2)^nu / Gamma(nu+1) omitted when nu not integral since not representable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN ibessel(GEN nu, GEN x, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: besselj(nu, x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bessel J function of index nu and argument x. If x converts to power series the initial factor (x/2)^nu / Gamma(nu+1) omitted when nu not integral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN jbessel(GEN nu, GEN x, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: besseljh(n, x)
rubrics_metrics.description: J-Bessel function of half-integral index: computes J_{n+1/2}(x) where n integer. Not very accurate when x small in current version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN jbesselh(GEN n, GEN x, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: besselk(nu, x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Modified Bessel K function of index nu and argument x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN kbessel(GEN nu, GEN x, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: besseln(nu, x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bessel N function of index nu and argument x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN nbessel(GEN nu, GEN x, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: cos(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cosine of x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gcos(GEN x, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: cosh(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hyperbolic cosine of x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gcosh(GEN x, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: cotan(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cotangent of x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gcotan(GEN x, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: dilog(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal branch of dilogarithm Li_2(x) defined by analytic continuation of power series sum_{n>=1} x^n / n^2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN dilog(GEN x, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: eint1(x, {n})
rubrics_metrics.description: Exponential integral E1(x) = integral_x^∞ e^{-t}/t dt extended to complex x != 0. If n present (integer) returns vector [eint1(x), ..., eint1(n x)] and values are correct up to bounded absolute error 10^{-n} (precision behavior special-cased).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When n omitted standard behavior with relative precision rules applies. Useful for L-function computations where absolute error control is needed. Library syntax: GEN veceint1(GEN x, GEN n = NULL, long prec) and GEN eint1(GEN x, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: erfc(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Complementary error function erfc(x) analytic continuation of (2/sqrt(pi)) integral_x^∞ e^{-t^2} dt to complex x != 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gerfc(GEN x, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: eta(z, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Variants of Dedekind's eta function. If flag=0 returns product_{n>=1} (1-q^n) (note missing q^{1/24} factor) with q determined by argument type: q = e^{2iπx} for complex x with positive imaginary part; q = x for p-adic or power series with positive valuation. If flag!=0 returns true η including q^{1/24} with complex conversion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN eta0(GEN z, long flag, long prec). Also GEN trueeta(GEN x, long prec) for flag=1.

rubrics_metrics.name: exp(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exponential function exp(x). p-adic arguments with positive valuation accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gexp(GEN x, long prec). For t_PADIC use GEN Qp_exp(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: expm1(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Return exp(x) - 1 computed to avoid catastrophic cancellation when x near 0; more accurate and often faster than exp(x)-1 for small x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only accepts real or complex arguments. Examples demonstrate speed and accuracy benefits. Library syntax: GEN gexpm1(GEN x, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: gamma(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Euler's Gamma function Γ(s) for complex s (pole at non-positive integers). For t_PADIC evaluates Morita gamma function (continuous p-adic extension).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show p-adic evaluation and usage with algdep. Library syntax: GEN ggamma(GEN s, long prec). For p-adic, GEN Qp_gamma(GEN x) available.

rubrics_metrics.name: gammah(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Gamma function evaluated at x + 1/2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN ggammah(GEN x, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: hyperu(a, b, x)
rubrics_metrics.description: U confluent hypergeometric function with parameters a, b (complex allowed) and argument x (implementation requires x positive).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN hyperu(GEN a, GEN b, GEN x, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: incgam(s, x, {g})
rubrics_metrics.description: Incomplete gamma function incgam(s,x) = integral_x^∞ t^{s-1} e^{-t} dt extended by analytic continuation to all complex x (s and x not both 0). Relative error bounded in terms of precision of s; if g provided and equals Γ(s) computation may be sped up for small |x|.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN incgam0(GEN s, GEN x, GEN g = NULL, long prec) and GEN incgam(GEN s, GEN x, long prec).
